claims.statement: The EU Data Act has applied since 12 September 2025 and gives business users access to raw data from connected products, including industrial machinery, and the ability to share it for more cost-effective repair and maintenance services.
European shortage reporting includes agricultural and industrial machinery mechanics, electrical mechanics, and electronics servicers among widespread shortage groups.
Better pre-visit data could stretch scarce specialist capacity by reducing diagnosis travel and wrong-parts calls, but this operational effect has not been demonstrated for a selected machine class.

contrary_evidence: The Data Act covers readily available product data, not every derived diagnostic insight, and permits restrictions for safety, security, and trade-secret protection.
OEM warranty terms, proprietary protocols, and existing CMMS or predictive-maintenance vendors may limit independent access or willingness to switch.
Supporting many machine brands too early would become a bespoke integration consultancy rather than a scalable product.

economics.acquisition_route: Independent service firms embed the owner-authorization link in their fault-intake form; once the owner approves sharing, the firm receives a standardized pre-visit packet and can resolve more calls without OEM portal hopping. Each service firm brings an installed customer base rather than the founder prospecting every factory individually.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Machine-class connectors, interpretation maps, verified fault-resolution playbooks, parts cross-references, and service-firm workflow integrations reduce pre-visit labor and repeat calls. The combination of connectivity and proven repair outcomes matters; raw machine data alone are neither exclusive nor sufficient.
fingerprint.customer: CEE food, packaging, and light-manufacturing plants with mixed-vendor connected compressors, chillers, palletizers, or packaging lines, together with independent maintenance firms serving those plants.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Independent service firms embed the owner-authorization link in their fault-intake form; once the owner approves sharing, the firm receives a standardized pre-visit packet and can resolve more calls without OEM portal hopping. Each service firm brings an installed customer base rather than the founder prospecting every factory individually.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Help the owner request authorized access, build narrowly scoped connectors for one machine class, normalize raw and metadata fields, detect known fault patterns, assemble parts and service context, and route unresolved cases to an independent or OEM technician. Start with diagnosis support, not autonomous safety decisions or a generic predictive-maintenance promise.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The plant pays an onboarding fee per supported machine class and a monthly fee per connected asset for normalized telemetry and triage; a maintenance firm can pay per diagnostic packet or resell the gateway with its service contract.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A recurring fault or expensive OEM callout occurs while raw machine data remain in separate vendor portals; the owner wants an independent maintainer to diagnose the asset using its Data Act access rights.

founder_fit: Excellent technical fit with data engineering, anomaly detection, AI-assisted manuals, and familiarity with FMCG operations.
Can begin part-time on one non-safety-critical machine class with independent service firms and low hardware spend.
Employer confidentiality and conflicts are serious; the founder must use only independently recruited customers, licensed data access, and no proprietary workplace knowledge.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Data-Act Maintenance Gateway for Mixed-Brand Factory Equipment
uncertainties: Which machine class exposes useful data with repeatable schemas and expensive enough failure events.
Actual response time and completeness of manufacturer data-access requests.
Measured reduction in truck rolls, diagnostic hours, downtime, and wrong-parts orders.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Recruit three independent service firms and five unrelated factories around one machine class, submit authorized data requests for ten assets, and create pre-visit packets for five real faults. Charge for at least three cases and compare visit count and diagnosis time with the firms' prior jobs; stop if data are inaccessible or do not change service effort.
